title: Halloweekend in Des Moines: Your Ultimate Guide to Spooky Events & Family Fun 2025
content:
When October rolls around in Central Iowa, Des Moines transforms into a Halloween wonderland that rivals any Midwest city. From spine-tingling haunted houses to family-friendly pumpkin patches, the capital city offers something for every ghoul, goblin, and ghost hunter. Whether you're a thrill-seeker looking for heart-pounding scares or a parent searching for wholesome autumn activities, this guide will help you navigate the best Halloween events Des Moines has to offer this season.

## The Most Terrifying Haunted Houses in Des Moines

Des Moines haunted houses have earned a reputation across Iowa for delivering legitimate scares that keep visitors coming back year after year. These aren't your average Halloween attractions—they're immersive experiences designed by local artists and horror enthusiasts who take their craft seriously.

### Sleepy Hollow: Iowa's Premier Haunted Attraction

Located just minutes from downtown Des Moines, Sleepy Hollow has been terrifying Central Iowa residents for over three decades. This legendary haunted attraction features multiple haunted houses, including the infamous "Nightmare on Hickman" and the claustrophobic "Buried Alive" experience. With over 40 actors bringing nightmares to life across 30,000 square feet of terror, Sleepy Hollow consistently ranks among the top haunted attractions in the Midwest.

**What to expect:**
- Four distinct haunted experiences in one location
- Professional makeup and special effects
- Interactive scares with live actors
- Extended hours during Halloweekend (October 27-31)
- VIP fast-pass options available for those who can't wait to be scared

### Haunted Basement at the Historic Salisbury House

For a uniquely Des Moines haunted experience, the Salisbury House in the historic Woodland Heights neighborhood transforms its basement into a chilling attraction each October. This 42-room mansion, built in the 1920s, provides an authentically eerie atmosphere that modern haunted houses simply can't replicate. The combination of genuine history and theatrical horror creates an unforgettable experience.

The Haunted Basement supports the preservation of this Des Moines landmark while delivering scares that play on the mansion's real history. Local actors volunteer their time to create an experience that's both educational and terrifying—a perfect blend of Iowa heritage and Halloween fun.

### Slaughterhouse Haunted Attraction

Situated in nearby Ankeny, Slaughterhouse lives up to its name with intense, adult-oriented horror that's not for the faint of heart. This attraction pushes boundaries with graphic scenes and aggressive actors who will test your courage. If you're seeking the most extreme haunted house experience in the Des Moines area, this is your destination.

**Important notes:**
- Recommended for ages 13 and up
- No touching policy (but actors can touch you)
- Not recommended for those with heart conditions or pregnant women
- Special "lights on" tours available for those who want to see the artistry without full scares

## Family-Friendly Halloween Activities Des Moines Families Love

Not everyone wants to be terrified during Halloween season, and Des Moines delivers plenty of wholesome, family-friendly options that capture the magic of autumn without the nightmares.

### Vander Veer Botanical Park's Boo at the Zoo

Blank Park Zoo transforms into a not-so-spooky wonderland each October with their annual Boo at the Zoo event. This beloved Des Moines tradition combines trick-or-treating with animal encounters, creating memories that last long after the candy is gone. Children can wear costumes while exploring the zoo, collecting treats at various stations, and participating in Halloween-themed activities.

**Highlights include:**
- Trick-or-treat stations throughout the zoo
- Costume parade and contest
- Pumpkin decorating stations
- Special animal enrichment activities with Halloween themes
- Photo opportunities with fall decorations
- Extended evening hours during Halloweekend

### Pumpkin Patches and Corn Mazes Near Des Moines

Central Iowa's agricultural heritage shines during autumn, with numerous family farms opening their doors for harvest celebrations. These working farms offer authentic Iowa experiences that connect families with the land.

#### Wilson's Orchard & Farm

Located in nearby Adel, Wilson's Orchard has been a Des Moines area favorite for generations. Their fall festival includes apple picking, a corn maze, pumpkin patch, and the famous apple cider donuts that people drive from across Iowa to taste. The farm's commitment to sustainable agriculture and community education makes every visit both fun and meaningful.

#### Bloomsbury Farm

This Atkins-based farm (about 45 minutes from Des Moines) offers an extensive corn maze that changes design each year, along with hayrides, a pumpkin patch, and farm animals. Their corn maze is one of the largest in Iowa, providing hours of entertainment for families willing to make the short drive from the Des Moines metro area.

#### Faulkner's Pumpkin Ranch

In nearby Grimes, Faulkner's offers a more intimate pumpkin patch experience with a focus on education. Children learn about pumpkin growing, farm life, and Iowa agriculture while selecting the perfect pumpkin. The ranch also features a small petting zoo and seasonal activities that change throughout October.

### Science Center of Iowa's Spooktacular Science

The Science Center of Iowa brings STEM education to Halloween with their annual Spooktacular Science event. This family-friendly celebration combines hands-on science experiments with Halloween themes, teaching children about the chemistry of candy, the physics of fear, and the biology of bats. It's an excellent option for families seeking educational entertainment in downtown Des Moines.

## Downtown Des Moines Halloween Events

The heart of Des Moines comes alive during Halloweekend with events that showcase the city's vibrant community spirit and creative energy.

### Court Avenue Halloween Block Party

Court Avenue, Des Moines' entertainment district, hosts one of Iowa's largest Halloween celebrations. This adult-oriented street party features costume contests with substantial cash prizes, live music from local bands, and special promotions at dozens of bars and restaurants. The energy on Court Avenue during Halloweekend is electric, with thousands of costumed revelers creating an unforgettable atmosphere.

**What to know:**
- Free admission to the street party
- Costume contest registration begins at 9 PM
- Multiple stages with live entertainment
- Special drink promotions at participating venues
- Enhanced security and police presence for safety
- Rideshare pickup zones designated throughout downtown

### East Village Trick-or-Treating

The East Village neighborhood embraces family-friendly Halloween with participating businesses offering treats to costumed children. This urban trick-or-treating experience allows families to explore one of Des Moines' most vibrant neighborhoods while collecting candy from local shops, galleries, and restaurants. It's a perfect way to support local Des Moines businesses while creating Halloween memories.

### Zombie Burger's Halloween Celebration

This iconic Des Moines restaurant goes all-out for Halloween, with special menu items, costume contests, and a festive atmosphere that captures the holiday's playful spirit. Located in the East Village, Zombie Burger has become a Halloween destination in its own right, with lines often stretching down the block during Halloweekend.

## Unique Des Moines Halloween Experiences

Beyond the traditional haunted houses and trick-or-treating, Des Moines offers distinctive Halloween experiences you won't find anywhere else in Iowa.

### Terrace Hill Candlelight Tours

The Iowa Governor's Mansion opens for special candlelight tours during October, offering a sophisticated Halloween experience. These guided tours explore the Victorian mansion's history, including ghost stories and unexplained phenomena reported over the years. The combination of authentic history, stunning architecture, and subtle spookiness creates an elegant alternative to traditional Halloween attractions.

### Des Moines Social Club's Halloween Bash

The Des Moines Social Club, housed in the historic Firehouse in the Western Gateway neighborhood, hosts an annual Halloween party that celebrates local arts and culture. This event features performances by Des Moines artists, DJs, costume contests, and an atmosphere that's more creative than scary. It's where Des Moines' artistic community comes together to celebrate Halloween with style.

### Haunted History Tours

Several local tour companies offer walking tours of downtown Des Moines that explore the city's darker history. These guided experiences visit historic buildings, discuss unsolved mysteries, and share ghost stories passed down through generations of Des Moines residents. Tours typically depart from the Court Avenue district and last approximately 90 minutes.

## Planning Your Perfect Halloweekend in Des Moines

Maximizing your Halloween experience in Des Moines requires some strategic planning, especially during the busy Halloweekend period when events overlap and crowds peak.

### Timing Your Visit

Most Des Moines Halloween events run throughout October, but Halloweekend (the Friday through Sunday before Halloween, plus Halloween night itself) offers the most concentrated selection of activities. Here's how to plan:

**Friday Night:** Start with dinner in the East Village, then head to one of the major haunted houses. Sleepy Hollow and Slaughterhouse both offer extended hours and typically have shorter lines early in the evening.

**Saturday:** Dedicate daytime hours to family-friendly activities like pumpkin patches or Boo at the Zoo. Evening options include the Court Avenue Halloween Block Party for adults or the Des Moines Social Club event for a more artistic vibe.

**Sunday:** Many families choose Sunday for a more relaxed pace, visiting the Science Center of Iowa or taking a haunted history tour. Several haunted attractions offer discounted Sunday tickets.

**Halloween Night:** If Halloween falls on a weekday, downtown Des Moines still celebrates with trick-or-treating in the East Village (typically 4-6 PM) and evening events at various venues.

### Transportation and Parking Tips

Navigating Des Moines during Halloweekend requires planning, especially in the downtown area where parking fills quickly.

- **Use rideshare services:** Uber and Lyft operate throughout Des Moines and are the safest option if you're visiting Court Avenue or other entertainment districts
- **Public parking ramps:** The city operates several parking ramps downtown with reasonable rates
- **DART bus service:** Des Moines Area Regional Transit offers routes throughout the metro area
- **Plan for traffic:** Popular haunted houses like Sleepy Hollow can have significant traffic backups on peak nights

### Ticket Purchasing Strategy

Many Des Moines Halloween events sell out or offer significant discounts for advance purchases:

- Purchase haunted house tickets online to skip box office lines
- Boo at the Zoo offers timed entry tickets that help manage crowds
- Some attractions offer combo tickets or season passes for multiple visits
- Follow Des Moines venues on social media for flash sales and promotional codes

## Safety Tips for Halloween in Des Moines

Ensuring a safe Halloween experience allows everyone to focus on fun. Des Moines is generally safe, but crowds and excitement require extra awareness.

### For Families

- Stick to well-lit areas when trick-or-treating
- Establish meeting points if you're visiting crowded venues like Boo at the Zoo
- Check all candy before allowing children to eat it
- Ensure costumes are visible to drivers with reflective tape or glow sticks
- Keep emergency contact information with children

### For Adults

- Designate a sober driver or use rideshare services
- Stay with your group in crowded areas like Court Avenue
- Keep valuables secure and be aware of your surroundings
- Respect haunted house rules and staff instructions
- Know your limits—some haunted attractions are genuinely intense

## Supporting Local Des Moines Businesses This Halloween

Halloween season provides an excellent opportunity to support the local businesses that make Des Moines special. Many of the events and attractions mentioned in this guide are operated by Des Moines residents who invest in our community year-round.

Consider purchasing costumes from local shops rather than national chains, dining at Des Moines restaurants before or after events, and sharing your experiences on social media to help promote these local businesses. The money you spend at local Des Moines establishments circulates through our community, supporting jobs and economic growth in Central Iowa.

## Making the Most of Your Des Moines Halloween Experience

Halloween in Des Moines offers something for everyone, from terrifying haunted houses that will test your courage to wholesome family activities that celebrate Iowa's agricultural heritage. The key to a perfect Halloweekend is matching activities to your interests and planning ahead to avoid crowds and sold-out events.

Whether you're a Des Moines resident looking to explore new Halloween traditions or a visitor discovering what Central Iowa has to offer, this Halloween season promises unforgettable experiences. The combination of Midwest hospitality, creative local talent, and genuine enthusiasm for the holiday makes Des Moines a Halloween destination worth celebrating.

Start planning your Halloweekend adventure today, and discover why Des Moines has become one of Iowa's premier Halloween destinations. From the historic streets of the East Village to the corn mazes of surrounding farmland, from spine-chilling haunted houses to family-friendly festivals, Des Moines delivers Halloween experiences that create lasting memories. This October, embrace the spooky season and explore everything Des Moines has to offer—you might just discover your new favorite Halloween tradition.
